newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo shares holds breath for bank,insurer merger.
newsitem.headline: Oslo shares holds breath for bank,insurer merger.

text.p: The Norwegian share market spent another flat session on Thursday with players waiting with bated breath to find out if the country's largest ever merger, between Christiania Bank of Kreditkasse and Storebrand, would go ahead.

Christiania Bank shareholders voted to approve the plans, but Storebrand's shareholders, who were due to begin meeting at 1600 GMT, were seen split. Both stocks closed higher with Christiania 0.20 crowns up at 24.50 crowns and Storebrand gaining 1.30 crowns to 47.10 crowns.
Dealers attributed Storebrand's 2.8 percent jump to investors swapping out of Christiania Bank on future arbitrage play between the two shares should the fusion go ahead.

A large block -- around seven percent of the Norwegian-owned part -- of stock moved in Scandinavian Airline Systems (SAS) accounting for 179 million crowns of business. Market sources were not immediately able to comment on the deal. SAS ended flat at 79 crowns.
Overall, the Total share index egded up a slim 0.37 percent to set a new all-time closing high at 1,188.01 points. Turnover was a moderate 836 million crowns.
